Travel and waiting are your estimates. Overnight shifts continue into the next day. Equal work times mean 24 hours. Add sleep or other commitments using the protected-time fields; a night shift does not mean your daytime is free.

What this can—and can’t—tell you

We compare published regular hours with your example week. The result minimizes overlap with work across the listed offices in your selection, using one-minute start times. Travel, visit length and waiting are assumptions, not observed times. Protected care time rules out a trip entirely; work time may overlap.

This is a possible time window, not a bookable appointment. Availability, queues, service cutoffs, holidays, eligibility and actual journey times can change it. Special-date hours are flagged separately. Office hours may cover several tasks with different requirements.

Time away from work does not necessarily mean lost pay. Paid leave, permission to switch shifts, and control over working time vary. An independent worker may choose their hours and still lose earnings. This model does not estimate either wages or the ability to take leave.

The dataset is a dated, partial inventory, not all NYC public services. Unverified hours are not treated as closed. Download source data · Full inventory and sources
